I’m a styling assistant, so my days are already hectic with fittings, pulls, last‑minute changes, but lately it’s like my mind never shuts up. I’ll start worrying about being late to a shoot, then I jump to thinking I’ll mess up the looks, then suddenly I’m picturing getting fired and not being able to pay rent. It just spirals like that over the smallest things.

Even when I’m home, I can’t really relax. I feel wired, like my body’s buzzing and I can’t sit still or properly unwind, even if I’m just watching TV. My shoulders, back, arms, even my legs feel constantly tight and sore, like I’ve done a workout when I haven’t. They tire out really easily when I’m carrying garment bags or standing all day on set.

There has been a lot going on with work and some personal stuff, but I’m not sure if this all started because of that or if it just kind of built up over time. It just feels like this background tension that’s always there.

I know work is stressful—tight deadlines, demanding clients, my boss snapping if a look isn’t perfect—but the worry isn’t just about that. Physically, I feel wired and tense all the time, like I’m wound up too tight. I can’t sit still in fittings; I’m always fidgeting. I’ll be driving and start obsessing about my mom getting sick, or my car breaking down, or whether I’m going to end up broke. Then it flips to, “What if I screwed up that IV last week?” or “What if I miss something on the next call?” Even on my days off, my brain just cycles through random worst‑case scenarios about my job, my bills, my health, my family—everything.

We did have a rough call about six months ago that’s been sitting with me, but honestly, this constant worrying was already there before that. The stress from the job just piles on top of what already feels like a baseline of anxiety.

Physically, I feel like I’m revved up all the time—on edge, jittery, can’t really relax, even when I’m just watching TV. But then, weirdly, I can sleep 10–12 hours and still feel like I could crash again. On my days off I’ll nap for hours and still wake up tired and wired at the same time.

My mind keeps spinning about that accident and about work in general—whether I missed something, whether the next call will be worse. Weirdly, I’m sleeping way more. If I’m not on shift, I can stay in bed 12 hours, nap during the day, but I still don’t feel rested. This has all been going on since within a few weeks of that call, and it hasn’t let up yet.
